source_text: Si ergo nolis esse contentiosus, puto quod iam videas quam recte intellegatur, quod aliter conaris exponere, quod propheta cum dixisset: Qui propitius fit omnibus iniquitatibus tuis [n157] ; quod fit utique remissione omnium peccatorum; continuo subiecit: Qui sanat omnes languores tuos [n158] ; ea mala volens intellegi, cum quibus donec sanentur, vel quantum possunt in hac vita magis magisque minuantur, non quiescunt intestina bella sanctorum.
pass_a_gloss: If then you should not wish to be contentious, I think that you now see how rightly it is understood, what you try to expound otherwise, that the prophet, when he had said: Who becomes propitious to all your iniquities; which happens certainly by the remission of all sins; at once added: Who heals all your languors; wishing those evils to be understood, with which, until they be healed, or as much as they can in this life be more and more diminished, the internal wars of the saints do not rest.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “So if you do not want to be contentious, I think you now see how rightly it is understood (though you try to explain it otherwise) that when the prophet had said, ‘Who is gracious to all your iniquities,’ which happens, of course, through the forgiveness of all sins, he at once added, ‘Who heals all your diseases’ (Psalm 103:3). By this he meant those evils with which the inner wars of the saints do not rest until they are healed, or, as far as they can be in this life, are lessened more and more.”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
